item.title: New Zealand passes law blocking climate action against companies: ‘dark day for democracy’
item.description: New Zealand has passed hotly contested legislation to block lawsuits that seek to hold companies liable for climate change harm. The right-wing coalition government’s legal amendment cleared a final hurdle in parliament on Tuesday night by a margin of 67 votes to 53. The law aimed to prevent civil litigation overriding its climate policy and undermining business confidence, the government said. It was introduced in response to a lawsuit filed by indigenous Maori climate activist Michael Smith... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: US vs ICC row escalates: Trump administration sanctions international court president, senior lawyer
item.description: In a significant escalation against the International Criminal Court (ICC), the United States has imposed sanctions on two prominent officials, including the ICC president and a senior trial lawyer. This move marks a continuation of the Trump administration's contentious stance towards the internationally recognized tribunal. The ICC criticized these sanctions as detrimental to the global legal framework, while several European allies voiced their concern over the U.S. actions. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Sacked Ukrainian defence minister calls for presidential election
item.description: Mykhailo Fedorov’s appeal is most direct challenge to Volodymyr Zelenskyy since Russian invasion in 2022 Ukraine’s recently dismissed former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov has called for a wartime presidential election in the most direct political challenge to Volodymyr Zelenskyy since the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022. The politician, whose abrupt sacking last month triggered a wave of protests , said that Ukraine had to “restore a full democratic process even amid a prolonged war” in a video address released online late on Tuesday evening. item.title: 2567 reproducciones · 59 reacciones | Exvocero avizora movilizaciones de sectores sociales por descontento y escándalos en el Gobierno de Paz Tras las duras declaraciones de la activista Nadia Beller, que involucran al Gobierno del presidente Rodrigo Paz y a su entorno cercano, el exvocero presidencial Alex Contreras advirtió sobre un posible escenario de movilizaciones de diversos sectores sociales una vez que concluya el periodo del estado de excepción. Según Contreras, el descontento ciudadano no respondería únicamente a las políticas económicas implementadas, sino también a la «falta de credibilidad» y a los constantes escándalos que rodean a la actual administración. “Les aseguro que, lamentablemente, el país puede volver a días de convulsión social una vez que concluya este estado de excepción”, advirtió en entrevista con la red ERBOL. item.title: Do not cut benefits for disabled young people, dozens of UK charities urge ministers
item.description: More than 40 charities write to Pat McFadden and review head Alan Milburn over fears of stricter eligibility rules More than 40 of the UK’s leading charities have warned ministers against imposing tougher benefit sanctions or cuts on disabled young people, as the government considers how to encourage more young people into work. The charities raised concerns that an imminent review of young people and work by Alan Milburn could bring in stricter eligibility rules for keeping disability benefits – or remove them altogether – as part of a wider plan to boost flagging youth job rates. item.title: Crisis en la FIFA: ¿quién es Kevin Lamour, el directivo francés destituido tras confrontar a Infantino?
item.description: El hasta ahora director de operaciones de la FIFA, Kevin Lamour, había denunciado el plan de Gianni Infantino para vender a inversores privados parte de los derechos comerciales del Mundial y otras competiciones. Su salida, semanas después de advertir que sus críticas podían costarle el puesto, profundiza una crisis que pone seriamente en duda la reelección del presidente del organismo. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Noboa se reúne con Xi en Beijing en una visita que busca acercar a Ecuador y a China
item.description: El presidente de Ecuador, Daniel Noboa, se encuentra en Beijing en un esfuerzo por acercarse a China sin entorpecer su relación con Estados Unidos. Ambos países mantienen una variada cooperación comercial desde 2024, pero Quito espera ampliar su colaboración a otros mercados, como la tecnología, la infraestructura, la energía y la educación. item.title: Pakistan top court orders ex-PM Imran Khan be moved to hospital from jail
item.description: Pakistan’s Supreme Court ordered on Tuesday that jailed former prime minister Imran Khan be moved to hospital for medical checks, after a petition by his lawyers over claims of poor health. Justice Shahid Waheed said 73-year-old Khan, who had been in jail since 2023 on corruption charges, would be shifted in the next two days to Shifa International Hospital in the capital Islamabad.
